requirements.title: Folder contract
requirements.text: Every deliverable lives under competition/<slug>/: code/<slug>.ipynb is the ONLY source artifact; datasets/ is read-only Kaggle data; train/ holds all run outputs; readme.md is the write-up. Never write outside the competition folder, never touch .engine/, frontend/data belongs to the report step only, and the legacy NTG/ folder does not exist (rule R10).

requirements.title: One notebook, top to bottom
requirements.text: code/<slug>.ipynb must run cleanly top-to-bottom on a fresh machine after `pip install -r requirements.txt`, kernel 'python3'. No manual steps, no hidden state between runs, no network access except reading ../datasets/, no uploads.

requirements.title: Determinism
requirements.text: One SEED constant at the top seeds python, numpy, sklearn, lightgbm, xgboost and catboost. The same commit and seed must reproduce the same CV score.

requirements.title: Honest measurement
requirements.text: Only report scores that were actually measured. The CV score comes from out-of-fold predictions, never from training-set predictions. Every run writes train/metrics.json (metric, task, cv_mean, cv_std, cv_folds, n_train, n_test, seed, n_splits, models, runtime_sec). A number that is not in an artifact is not a result.

requirements.title: Score matching gate
requirements.text: A competition counts as solved only when the OOF score meets the target score (default: user-set or leaderboard-derived; recorded per competition in the engine store). Always record the CV-vs-leaderboard gap; if the gap is large (> 2x the CV std), diagnose the split (duplicates, group leakage, distribution shift) BEFORE adding more models.

requirements.title: Leakage discipline
requirements.text: No target-dependent transform may run before the split. Target/category encodings must be fold-safe (computed excluding the row's own fold). Assert every training row received exactly one OOF prediction. Use group-aware or time-aware folds when ids or timestamps make random folds leak.

requirements.title: Optimization ladder
requirements.text: Improve in this order and stop when the gate is met: (1) clean leak-free baseline, (2) sanity-check folds and metric implementation, (3) domain feature engineering from the problem statement, (4) model zoo — LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, (5) OOF-fitted ensemble (rank-mean for rank-based metrics, hill-climb weights otherwise), (6) fold-safe target encodings, (7) pseudo-labelling / self-training, (8) bounded hyperparameter search with a fixed seed budget. Never jump to (8) before (1)–(4).

requirements.title: Resource budget
requirements.text: CPU only by default. One notebook execution must finish within ENGINE_NOTEBOOK_TIMEOUT (default 1h). Subsample while iterating, use the full dataset on the final attempt. A cycle makes at most ENGINE_MAX_ATTEMPTS coder attempts.

requirements.title: Submission policy
requirements.text: Notebooks never upload anything. Submissions go through the engine, only when ENGINE_SUBMIT_ENABLED=1, respecting daily submission limits, and every submission is logged in the engine store.

requirements.title: Legacy folder
requirements.text: The NTG/ folder is a historical trial-and-error workspace. Never read from it, never write to it, never reference its contents in prompts, code or reports.

requirements.title: README write-up
requirements.text: competition/<slug>/readme.md must contain: (a) problem summary and metric and why it matters, (b) algorithm walkthrough — features, folds, models, ensemble, (c) the score table copied from train/metrics.json — OOF mean/std/folds, leaderboard, target, gap, (d) what was tried and rejected with numbers, (e) ranked next steps. Never paste a score that is not in an artifact.

requirements.title: Security
requirements.text: Never hard-code, print or commit credentials. Kaggle access comes from env vars or ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json only. No secrets in notebooks, READMEs, logs or synced data. Datasets/ and train/ artifacts never enter git (.gitignore enforces it).

requirements.title: Reproducible artifacts
requirements.text: Every executed attempt leaves behind: train/metrics.json, train/submission.csv (when produced), train/oof_<model>.csv, train/importance_<model>.csv, the trained model itself (train/model.joblib — the fitted estimators, so every notebook ships a loadable model and not just a score), the executed notebook copy, and the attempt log — so any number in the README can be traced to its run.

pipeline.description: Fetch problem statement, metric, file list and dataset profile (engine/scout.py)
Enforce the folder contract and materialise a runnable baseline (engine/templates.py)
Trigger OpenCode to write/repair the notebook under the rulebook (engine/opencode_runner.py)
Run the notebook top-to-bottom, keep a partial copy on failure (engine/notebook_runner.py)
Read train/metrics.json and compare against the gate; never invent a number (engine/scorer.py)
Feed the gap back and climb the R7 ladder, at most ENGINE_MAX_ATTEMPTS times (engine/orchestrator.py)
Write train/report.md and refresh the frontend dashboard (engine/report.py)
